sections.h2: Selling routes for an Anna homeowner
sections.html:
Three paths are open: an agent listing, a sale you run yourself, or a direct cash offer. The tradeoff is price against speed. Anna lies in north central Collin County, and its population roughly doubled in five years. Many sellers there own newer houses in subdivisions where builders are still active.

That shapes the sale. Anyone weighing your resale against a builder's model down the street will look hard at the price, the condition and any recurring assessment on the tax bill. Cash buyers skip that comparison and make an offer for the house in its present state.

  • List with an agent if the home is clean and newer and you have time to wait for a financed buyer.
  • Go without an agent only if drafting the contract and handling title paperwork feels manageable.
  • Take cash when the move is urgent, the house was inherited, a tenant is involved, or you do not want to fund repairs.

Few places in Collin County are growing faster than Anna. It counted 8,249 people in 2010 and 16,896 in 2020, then reached an estimated 35,245 by mid-2025, a gain of 105.7% measured from the 2020 starting estimate.

Households here are big and young, and the average commute runs 30.7 minutes. The typical buyer is a family wanting space within reach of McKinney and the Dallas job market. Because so much of Anna was built recently, sale questions usually involve expired builder warranties, drainage on newly graded lots and neighborhood-level assessments.

sections.h2: Public improvement districts and special assessments
sections.html:
They can raise what a buyer pays every year. Anna's City Council forms public improvement districts by resolution. One example is Resolution 2023-02-1378, approved February 14, 2023, which created The Woods at Lindsey Place Public Improvement District. A district lets a city pay for streets, utilities and similar improvements through assessments on the lots that benefit.

Collin County also has many municipal utility districts and water districts, and each shows up as a separate taxing entity. A house inside one has an extra line on the property tax bill.

  • Have the title company check whether the lot lies inside a public improvement district or a utility district.
  • Ask the Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector which entities appear on your tax statement.
  • If the lot is in a district, ask the city for the assessment schedule.
  • Share those figures with the buyer early, so the price talk uses the true yearly cost.

Anna's Building Department handles both. It operates from the Municipal Complex at 120 W. 7th Street, Suite 142, on weekdays from eight to five, and its phone number is 972-924-2616. The city publishes requirements for fences, irrigation, remodels, roofing, solar panels, pools and spas, water heaters and patio covers.

Request an inspection by email before 4 p.m. the business day ahead; none take place on weekends or holidays. Certain jobs need extra forms such as a site drainage acknowledgement, a homeowner's affidavit or a pool affidavit.

Prior to listing, make sure each fence, pool, roof or remodel you added was permitted and passed its final inspection. Inspectors working for buyers ask about this, and a missing final can hold up the closing.

Billing comes from the Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector. October statements are due as soon as you receive them, and anything paid after January 31 draws penalties. The year's lien takes effect January 1, which is why a title company will deduct any unpaid balance from your proceeds.

The 2023 table from Collin CAD showed these exemptions for Anna city. A new table is posted each year, so confirm the current entries.

  • Homestead: 3.00% of value, with a $5,000 floor.
  • Age 65 or older: $30,000.
  • Disabled person: $30,000.

A buyer who moves in mid-year may be able to claim the homestead exemption for the remainder of that year when the previous owner never had one. School taxes are capped for owners with an age or disability exemption, and the cap can travel with them to another Texas home, stated as a percentage.

Appraisals on a homestead may climb no more than 10% a year, not counting new improvements. For that reason a long-time owner's bill can lag well behind market price.

The filings go through Collin County offices, and the Texas rules are short.

  • Heirs: if your name is not on the recorded deed, you can still get the homestead exemption by giving the district a sworn statement of ownership, a death certificate and a recent utility bill. An estate that holds real property beyond the homestead cannot use the small-estate route.
  • Lender action: the borrower has 20 days from the default letter to cure, and the lender must give notice of sale 21 days or more ahead of the first-Tuesday auction.
  • Deeds: bring the Collin County Clerk an original or a certified copy, signed and notarized.

If the clock is running, closing ahead of the auction keeps the timeline in your hands. With no loan to approve, a cash purchase can compress the schedule.

sections.h2: From contract to closing in Collin County
sections.html:
Accepting an offer sends the file to a title company. Staff there order a tax certificate, request payoff statements from every lender, and search for liens, open permits and assessments on the lot. If the buyer needs a mortgage, an appraisal and underwriting lengthen the calendar. Paying cash eliminates both.

You sign the deed in front of a notary at closing, and it is then sent to the county clerk. The appraisal district later updates the owner of record, and the new owner applies for a homestead exemption in their own name during the January through April window. File away the settlement statement, a copy of the deed, and any receipt proving the year's tax was paid.

sections.h2: Preparing an Anna house for a quick sale
sections.html:
Newer houses move fastest when the paperwork is ready to hand over. Pull together the settlement statement from your own purchase, any builder warranty papers still in force, and your latest tax statement. Note each special district that bills the lot and its annual cost. A buyer who sees those numbers on day one has less reason to reopen the price after an inspection.

Leaving for a new job or a family move? Share your deadline with the buyer. Cash buyers can often meet it, since no lender must sign off and title work begins the day the contract is signed.

faqs.a: The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 35,245 residents, more than double the 2020 estimates base of 17,137. The city has 16.45 square miles of land.

faqs.q: Is a PID assessment passed to the buyer when I sell an Anna house?
faqs.a: Yes, an assessment attached to the lot stays with the property. Ask the title company and the city for the schedule, and share it with buyers up front.

faqs.q: Which county office collects tax for Anna?
faqs.a: The Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector bills and collects. Collin Central Appraisal District, in McKinney, sets the value and processes exemptions.

faqs.q: Should I gather permit records before listing in Anna?
faqs.a: No law requires it, but buyers and inspectors ask. Anna's Building Department can tell you which permits were issued and whether they were finaled.

faqs.q: Can an heir claim the homestead exemption on an inherited Anna house?
faqs.a: Yes. An heir not named on a recorded deed files an affidavit of ownership interest with the appraisal district, along with the death certificate and a recent utility bill.
